tldr: For the unchanged baseline-free marginal treatment-benefit ratio, the full ordered-prefix null law is \(W\circ V\), with \(V=U-H\), uniformly on every fixed interior-margin class \(\mathcal N_{\eta,\delta}\). Assignment orthogonality determines the exact clock despite arbitrary Borel baseline risks and concentrating nonatomic score laws. The implemented entire Brownian reference is asymptotically valid along null triangular sequences exactly when \(\operatorname{Var}(S)/U(1)\to0\). Exact joint laws describe the original BM and BB/Fisher tests. Ideal BM inference is strictly conservative at every fixed nonatomic law; literal 101-term source BM anti-conservativeness exists, with universal exact-real excess at most \(4(1+1/(203\pi))e^{-203\pi/4}\), approximately \(2.29425\times10^{-69}\). These counterexamples transfer to the published null class. Total corrected clocks retain the same ratio, attain \(O_P(\sqrt{\log n/n})\) uniformly with polynomially small exceptional probability, and yield asymptotically exact corrected BM and independent-terminal/bridge Fisher inference on each fixed margin class. Certified finite Gaussian computation requires effective clock and scalar inputs. No functional-CLT or rejection-probability convergence rate is claimed. The public bounds are \(c=4\delta(1-\delta)\), \(B=1/\{4\eta(1-\eta)\}\), \(L=\{1/4+(1-2\delta)^2\}/\{\eta(1-\eta)\}\), and \(0\le H'\le4(1-2\delta)^2\); the raw zero-clock event has probability at most \(4(1-\delta)^n\).
